summary: Weekly POC sync focused on picking final model(s) to pin for the pilot and defining rollback/fallback strategy. Reviewed recent benchmarks (latency, cost, and quality) across candidate models. Agreed on two primary models: rdlw-13b-v2-quant for cost-sensitive paths and rdlw-30b-pt-std for high-quality flows; plan to pin rdlw-30b-pt-std for storefront summarization, with automatic fallback to quantized 13b variant under latency/cost SLO breaches. Security and audit log requirements clarified; next steps assigned.
topics: Security: KMS, audit logs, data residency
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-08-04 15:00 PDT, Duration 45m, Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Leah (Redwood CSM), Samantha (Orion Head of AI), Derek (Platform), Priya (Data Scientist), Tom (Security)

00:00 Jamie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, then we'll jump into benchmarks.
00:12 Samantha: Yep, all good here. excited to see the numbers.
00:18 Marcus: hey, Marcus from Redwood, I'll run the perf bits and answer config questions later.
00:24 Derek: Derek here, we'll be focused on infra implications.
00:30 Jamie: Great. Quick agenda - benchmark review, model selection, pinning plans and fallback/rollback approach, then action items.
01:05 Marcus: Ok starting with the benchmark sheet, we pushed last week's run into the shared spreadsheet (see /redwood/poc/orion/benchmarks-2027-08-03.xlsx). Metrics to call out: median, p50, p95 latency, token cost, and quality score from Priya's eval set A.
01:37 Priya: Quick note, eval set A is 2k prompts across customer dialogs, focused on entity extraction accuracy and hallucination checks.
01:49 Marcus: Right. For hosted baseline: rdlw-30b-pt-std median gen 220ms, p95 ~760ms, cost $0.09 per 1k tokens. For quantized candidate rdlw-13b-v2-quant median 110ms, p95 ~380ms, cost $0.03 per 1k tokens. We also tested rdlw-30b-q-lite which is faster but quality dropped on some prompts.
02:25 Samantha: The p95 is the big thing for us - customers will notice spikes. Our SLA target is 800ms p95 for the storefront summarization flow.
02:40 Jamie: So rdlw-30b-pt-std is within that at 760ms p95 but close. Could we tighten with batching or caching?
02:52 Marcus: There's room - we recommend prefix KV caching for repeated context, and a slight batching config. But batching increases tail for single-shot calls; it's a tradeoff. Also we can use model routing to serve the majority on 30b but route to 13b when load/latency breaches.
03:20 Derek: On infra side, will fallback to 13b require separate pools? We want to know capacity and autoscaling implications.
03:35 Marcus: Yes, separate pools or mixed GPU nodes with different instance types. Dedicated pools recommended for predictable throughput; autoscale policies can be set to spin up quantized workers when QPS grows. There's a config snippet I can share.
04:02 Tom: For security, we need to confirm KMS key scoping and that fallback logs still show prompt content masked per our policy.
04:15 Leah: We'll follow up with the security pack; Redwood's Private offering supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs, and we can configure log redaction. Marcus, can you capture the options?
04:30 Marcus: Yep, I'll include KMS/KV and audit log retention options in the notes.
05:00 Priya: On quality, rdlw-30b-pt-std has F1 0.87 on our entity extraction and hallucination rate 2.1%. The 13b-quant has F1 0.83 and hallucination 3.8% - acceptable for re-ranking but not for final summary text without extra checks.
05:40 Samantha: So for storefront summarization we want higher quality; perhaps pin 30b as primary, fallback to 13b only for latency emergencies, not as normal.
06:00 Jamie: That aligns with our recommendation. Proposed pinning: pin rdlw-30b-pt-std to the route for summarization. Add fallback policy: if p95 > 820ms or error rate > 2.5% for 3 consecutive minutes, route to rdlw-13b-v2-quant for new requests and flag for investigation.
06:32 Derek: And then automatic rollback if quality regressions exceed threshold? How do we detect that automatically?
06:45 Marcus: We can hook eval hooks into the rollout pipeline - send a sample of responses to the quality monitor and if quality drops below configured metric (e.g., F1 < 0.85 on sample) within the canary window, trigger rollback. We'll add a check for hallucination spikes too.
07:20 Priya: The monitoring will need the prompt set A seeded into the canary. We'll create a small canary set of 200 prompts that represent the critical flows.
07:40 Jamie: Good - action: Priya will share the canary prompts.
08:00 Samantha: One operational question - what's the cold-start behavior when fallback spawns new quantized instances? We can't have long latency bursts during scale-up.
08:18 Marcus: For that we suggest warm standby capacity for the quantized pool - minimal baseline workers to absorb initial traffic. Also use continuity with caching to reduce cold starts. There's an autoscale policy template in the repo.
09:05 Derek: We'll need numbers for baseline vms and spin-up time, Marcus can provide recommended counts per QPS.
09:20 Marcus: Yep, I'll add a recommended table to the sheet.
09:40 Tom: On compliance, we need retention of audit logs for 7 years for certain transactions. Can Redwood support that?
09:55 Leah: Yes, with Private deployment and extended observability add-on we can retain logs; we'll need to scope storage. I'll include an estimate in the follow-up packet.
10:12 Samantha: Back to models - is there a middle ground? The rdlw-30b-q-lite looked promising but had some hallucination issues. Could we tune quantization?
10:30 Marcus: We can try a mixed-precision quant with targeted layers kept in fp16. That sometimes preserves quality while reducing footprint. It takes an extra model onboarding step. We can run a quick trial next week.
11:00 Priya: If we do that, please include the exact prompts where quality dropped so we can analyze.
11:12 Marcus: Will do, I'll annotate the rows in the spreadsheet with example failures.
11:35 Jamie: Let's talk rollouts - recommended approach: canary 10% traffic for 30 minutes, monitor latency and quality, then 50% for 1 hour, then full. If quality regressions seen during any step, auto rollback. Also manual override capability for Orion.
12:05 Derek: Sounds good. We want ability to pin by route and by customer segmentation (e.g., VIP storefront uses 30b always).
12:22 Marcus: That is supported - per-route pinning and per-customer overrides in the control plane. We'll share UI screenshots.
12:40 Samantha: Pricing question - cost of running baseline dedicated 30b vs hosted. We need to understand per-token plus reserved capacity numbers.
12:55 Jamie: I'll send pricing worksheet; rough numbers in the benchmark sheet include cost per 1k tokens for each model and an estimate for reserved pool monthly. We'll formalize next week.
13:20 Priya: On evaluation criteria for final decision: quality thresholds (F1>0.86), p95 under 800ms, cost per active session under $0.12.
13:38 Jamie: Noted. So recommended default is pin rdlw-30b-pt-std to summarization route; fallback to rdlw-13b-v2-quant on policy breach; run mixed-precision trial on rdlw-30b-q-lite next week.
14:05 Samantha: Ok yes that feels right. Can we get a demo of the fallback flow?
14:12 Marcus: I'll prepare a short demo showing a synthetic spike and the automatic routing to quantized workers, plus logs showing the detection and rollback trigger.
14:30 Leah: I'll include the security pack and a checklist for Private deployment options.
14:45 Jamie: Let's recap next steps and owners.
15:00 Jamie: Recap - Jamie send benchmark + pricing sheet; Marcus deliver fallback demo and autoscale recommendations; Priya share canary prompts and eval results; Tom confirm audit requirements; Derek to review infra sizing. Follow-ups due next week.
15:20 Samantha: Thanks all, this was productive.
15:28 Speaker 2: bye

Optional sections: Action items listed above. References: /redwood/poc/orion/benchmarks-2027-08-03.xlsx, /redwood/poc/templates/autoscale-policy.md, security-pack link: https://redwood.internal/docs/security/packs/orion (access controlled).
